newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks higher, market seen as stable.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks higher, market seen as stable.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly higher on Friday and traders expected the stable trend to continue at least for a week.
But some predicted publishing of the list of firms included in the mass privatisation scheme could significantly influence market activity.
"Firms on the list should then fall, and others will rise," said Igor Kos of brokerage Taurus. The list is to be published later this month.
He predicted further growth for confectioner Kras amid rumours its shares would not be listed for free voucher distribution.
* Of eight active issues, six rose, one fell and one was unchanged.
* Pliva rose 200 kuna, closing at 12,200, with 394 shares changing hands.
* Most actively traded Zagrebacka Banka gained 15 kuna to close at 750, with 9,728 shares sold. It today reported a group pre-tax profit of 107 million for the first half of the year.
* Of hoteliers that traded three were gainers:
-- Istraturist added 20 kuna to 160, on volume of 5 shares, Jadranturist 13 kuna to 178 on volume of 586 shares and Laguna inched up two kuna to close at 820, with 365 shares sold.
-- Riviera was the only loser dipping 11 kuna to 89, on volume of 49 shares.
* Confectioner Kras added 30 kuna to close at a new high of 350 kuna on volume of 968 shares.
* Food processor Podravka traded flat at 225 kuna, selling 1,745 shares.
* Daily volume higher at 13,840 shares, daily turnover four times higher at 13.1 million kuna. Total weekly turnover slightly lower at 23.2 million kuna.
* Central bank's exchange rate: 5.3639 kuna = $1. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
